parsed.summary: Tracing the drawing against the specification, the power tree (F1/D2/T3 input, U1 TPS62933 24V→5V with R14=52k3/R15=10k giving ~4.98V, U2 AZ1117 5V→3V3), the I2C topology (isolated pH/EC via U3/U4 ADM3260 with PDIS on pin 8, unisolated EZO-RTD on the main bus, 2k2 pull-ups), the three TMC2209 drivers (STEP lines on IO10/11/15/19, shared STEP_BUS, 110 mΩ sense resistors, per-driver 5VOUT→VREF dividers), the main-pump/ATO switches (T2 IRLR2905, AON6407 low-side, 100Ω gates, SS34 flybacks, 4k7/10k float interlocks) and the DNP/unwired parts (PR1 LiDAR free, PR5/PR6 crossed out) all match the intended design. The remaining differences I found – the ESP32 pin labels for ATO_VALVE/EZO_PDIS and the fact that the ATO-valve MOSFET carries reference T5 (AON6407) while an extra AON6407 sits at T3 in the input path with no AO3400A present – are either behaviorally benign (the ATO valve is still driven by a suitable N-MOSFET; the added series MOSFET implements the README's reverse-polarity feature) or fall squarely under the specification's explicitly documented 'firmware GPIO map does not match the r2 schematic' limitation, which must not be reported. I therefore find no deviation that would make the board behave differently from the intended design.
